_note: Sample questions only. In each entry the first option is the correct one; every attempt shuffles the options. A module's quiz draws from `poolSize` consecutive questions starting at its `questionOffset` (wrapping around).

bank.text: What left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) defines heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)?
bank.explanation: HFrEF is LVEF of 40% or less. 41–49% is mildly reduced and 50% or more is preserved.

bank.text: Which set lists the four foundational drug groups in HFrEF?
options: ARNI (or ACE-I/ARB), beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor
Loop diuretic, digoxin, nitrate, calcium-channel blocker
bank.explanation: The four pillars are RAS inhibition with ARNI, an evidence-based beta-blocker, an MRA and an SGLT2 inhibitor.

bank.text: Sacubitril/valsartan combines a neprilysin inhibitor with which drug?
bank.explanation: Valsartan is the ARB component of the ARNI.

bank.text: A patient taking an ACE inhibitor is to start sacubitril/valsartan. What is the minimum washout?
bank.explanation: Stop the ACE inhibitor at least 36 hours before the first ARNI dose because of the risk of angioedema.

bank.text: Which beta-blockers have proven mortality benefit in HFrEF?
bank.explanation: Only these three have outcome trials in HFrEF.

bank.text: Which tests are essential after starting or increasing an MRA?
bank.explanation: MRAs can raise potassium and creatinine, so check both within the first weeks.

bank.text: SGLT2 inhibitors such as dapagliflozin and empagliflozin reduce HF events in HFrEF:
bank.explanation: The benefit in HFrEF is independent of diabetes status.

bank.text: A patient is breathless at rest. Which NYHA class is this?
bank.explanation: NYHA IV means symptoms at rest or with any physical activity.

bank.text: Which blood test is commonly used to help rule out heart failure when the value is low?
bank.explanation: Natriuretic peptides rise with ventricular wall stress; a low value makes heart failure unlikely.

bank.text: In HFrEF, loop diuretics are mainly used to:
bank.explanation: Diuretics control fluid but have not been shown to improve survival.

bank.text: Ivabradine may be considered when a patient is in sinus rhythm with LVEF of 35% or less and:
options: Resting heart rate is 70 bpm or more despite maximum tolerated beta-blocker
The patient cannot take any beta-blocker and is hypotensive
bank.explanation: Ivabradine lowers heart rate in sinus rhythm and is added on top of a maximally tolerated beta-blocker.

bank.text: An ICD for primary prevention is generally considered when LVEF is:
options: 35% or less after at least 3 months of optimal medical therapy
Reduced during an acute admission only
bank.explanation: Reassess LVEF on optimal therapy before deciding on a primary-prevention ICD.

bank.text: Which patient is the best candidate for cardiac resynchronisation therapy (CRT)?
options: LVEF 35% or less, sinus rhythm and left bundle branch block with QRS 150 ms or more
bank.explanation: CRT benefit is greatest with LBBB and a wide QRS.

bank.text: Which of these should usually be avoided in a patient with HFrEF?
bank.explanation: NSAIDs cause sodium and water retention and can worsen heart failure and kidney function.

bank.text: A patient on an MRA has a serum potassium of 5.8 mmol/L. What is the right next step?
options: Reduce or stop the MRA and recheck potassium urgently
Continue unchanged and repeat in 3 months
bank.explanation: Potassium above 5.5 mmol/L needs the MRA dose reduced or stopped and close monitoring.

bank.text: How should a beta-blocker be started in HFrEF?
options: In a stable, euvolaemic patient at a low dose, then up-titrated
At full dose during acute decompensation
Only after all other drugs are at target
bank.explanation: Start low, go slow, and avoid starting during acute congestion.

bank.text: The 1-minute sit-to-stand test (1MSTS) measures:
options: Lower-limb functional capacity, as repetitions in 60 seconds
bank.explanation: The number of chair stands in one minute is a simple measure of functional capacity.

bank.text: In the ACC/AHA classification, Stage C heart failure means:
options: Structural heart disease with current or previous symptoms
Risk factors only, no structural disease
bank.explanation: Stage C patients have structural disease and have had symptoms of heart failure.

bank.text: Hydralazine with isosorbide dinitrate is mainly used in HFrEF:
options: When ACE-I, ARB and ARNI cannot be used or are not tolerated
As first-line therapy for all patients
bank.explanation: It is an alternative for patients who cannot take RAS inhibitors, for example because of renal failure or hyperkalaemia.

bank.text: Which approach to GDMT is recommended?
options: Start all four pillars early at low doses, then titrate
Maximise one drug fully before starting the next
Wait for symptoms to worsen before adding drugs
Start only drugs that lower blood pressure
bank.explanation: Rapid sequencing of all four pillars improves outcomes more than slow, one-at-a-time optimisation.
